name: network and transport
reason: Transport factors with no artefact that states a procedure and an oracle for them. Framing and cache keying are the two areas this repo does cover; the rest of the stack, particularly QUIC, WebTransport, TURN and IP options, is unaddressed.

L02-001.note: Desync detection exists precisely because two parsers disagree about the request boundary. Both tools state preconditions and a confirmation oracle.

L02-002.note: The TE.TE obfuscation variants touch header folding, but the entry does not isolate folding as the factor under test.

L02-003.note: CL.TE and TE.CL are exactly the duplicate and conflicting header cases, with a stated detection oracle.

L02-004.note: The core smuggling class. The entries state the precondition (both headers accepted) and the oracle (a smuggled prefix that becomes a second request).

L02-005.note: Chunk size obfuscation is one of the documented TE.TE variants the tools test.

L02-006.note: The framing specification names the normalisation question. It is a reference, not a procedure.

L02-008.note: Desync is only observable because connections are reused across clients, and the tools require that condition to demonstrate the effect.

L02-009.note: Timeout asymmetry is a condition the tool assumes rather than a factor it tests.

L02-010.note: Pipelining is a precondition of some variants, not the object of a test.

L02-011.note: h2c upgrade smuggling is the cleartext downgrade case, and the tool states what a positive looks like.

L02-012.note: HTTP/2 specific header handling is the mechanism of the h2 desync classes the tool implements.

L02-013.note: The specification states the rule. No artefact tests whether a given hop enforces it.

L02-014.note: Stream concurrency is described in the specification entry and untested by any artefact here.

L02-015.note: Reset semantics appear in the h2 research the entry links to, without a procedure for the factor.

L02-016.note: HPACK state is not addressed anywhere. A compression oracle at the header layer is entirely absent.

L02-021.note: Fingerprinting observes the negotiated surface, which implies the termination topology without testing it.

L02-022.note: Subdomain enumeration finds SNI routed hosts. It does not test whether routing keys on the server name.

L02-024.note: JA3 and JA4 fingerprint the client hello. Negotiation of version and cipher is not the same question, so this names the area without testing it.

L02-028.note: Recon enumerates answers. The resolution path and which resolver is authoritative is untouched.

L02-029.note: Dangling record takeover is adjacent to rebinding and is not the same test.

L02-031.note: Takeover detection walks CNAMEs to a claimable target, which is one use of chain handling.

L02-033.note: The cache scanner tests whether freshness is honoured as declared, with a stated oracle.

L02-034.note: Key composition is the central question of cache testing, and mitmproxy is the entry that gives byte control to vary one property at a time.

L02-035.note: Normalisation before keying is one of the classes the scanner reports.

L02-036.note: Unkeyed input is the poisoning mechanism, and curl is named as the way to read the cache headers that confirm a hit.

L02-037.note: Invalidation on write is not a class the scanner tests.

L02-038.note: Where normalisation happens is the difference between the two parsers, and the tool's oracle depends on it.

L02-039.note: Hop by hop stripping failure is a documented smuggling precondition the tools test for.

L02-040.note: Payload obfuscation against an edge touches header handling, not the trust chain for client address.

L02-042.note: No entry covers WebSocket at all. D11 named WebSocket in its title while holding no WebSocket entry, which is corrected in the domain file.

L02-045.note: No entry covers server-sent events. Reconnect semantics and Last-Event-ID trust are unaddressed.

L02-047.note: Browser scenario capture can observe candidate gathering. It is a capture tool, not a leak test.

L02-053.note: Zeek is the artefact that would answer whether a request is visible. No entry states how to test coverage.

L02-058.note: Impersonation controls the client hello fingerprint. Whether a defender's policy keys on it is untested here.

L02-060.note: Fingerprinting reads error surfaces. Mapping which hop produces which error is not a stated test.
